title: RBAC v2 evidence access model and workflows
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposed RBAC v2-based access model and the associated control evidence workflows for Redwood's evidence automation system. Focus: how role/attribute claims interact with evidence producers/collectors, audit log schema extensions to carry provenance and access metadata, SIEM export filters tied to RBAC-derived scopes, and retention/gating rules for control evidence.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Mapping RBAC v2 roles and attributes to evidence consumer permissions
- Audit event schema fields required to represent evidence provenance and access decisions
- Collector behavior when enforcing RBAC-derived access boundaries
- SIEM export rules that respect per-customer / per-tenant evidence scoping
- Control evidence lifecycle: creation, access, attestation, archival, purge

Non-goals:
- Full RBAC v2 design (assume RBAC v2 spec exists separately)
- Network-level access controls (handled by Private deployment docs)

Background / motivation:
We are moving from a coarse RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 (attribute-backed) to allow granular evidence access without adding ad-hoc ACLs in each collector. Evidence automation currently stores artifacts in tenant buckets and emits audit events, but consumers (SRE, Compliance, External auditors) need to be allowed/restricted based on roles, project attributes, and control ownership. Without explicit policy in the evidence layer, we end up with shadow ACLs and manual processes. RBAC v2 should be the single source of truth for who can read/download/attest evidence.

Goals:
- Define how RBAC v2 attributes map to evidence permissions (read, download, attest, revoke, transfer)
- Extend audit log schema to carry "evidence_scope" and "evidence_provenance" fields
- Ensure SIEM export respects tenant scoping and role-based filtering (no leakage)
- Provide deterministic collector behavior for access-denied cases (e.g., redact, mask, or drop export)
- Document operational workflows and edge cases for control evidence lifecycle

High-level model:
- Principal: an authenticated identity that contains RBAC claims (roles and attributes). Examples: user:alice@example.com, svc:collector-1@redwood.local
- Resource: evidence artifact with metadata: evidence_id, control_id, tenant_id, evidence_tier, retention_policy
- Permission actions: evidence:read, evidence:download, evidence:attest, evidence:archive, evidence:delete
- Policy evaluation: RBAC v2 policy engine evaluates principal claims + resource attributes to return allow/deny + obligations (e.g., must_mask, must_log)

Example role->permission mappings (suggested):
- role:control-owner (scope: control_id) => evidence:read, evidence:attest, evidence:download
- role:tenant-auditor (scope: tenant_id, auditor:boolean) => evidence:read (view-only, no download)
- role:sec-ops (global with justification tag) => evidence:read, evidence:download (must_mask=PII)
- role:svc-collector (service identity) => evidence:write, evidence:append

Attribute-based constraints to use frequently:
- control_id (string)
- tenant_id (UUID)
- evidence_tier (low|sensitive|high)
- retention_days (int)
- must_mask (boolean) - derived obligation from policy

Audit event schema extensions (new fields to add to our audit logs emitted by collectors and the platform audit middleware):
- evidence_id: string (stable artifact id)
- evidence_version: string (semantic or timestamp)
- control_id: string
- evidence_tier: string
- resource_tenant: string
- access_decision: allow|deny
- decision_reason: short code (e.g., RBAC_DENY_SCOPE_MISMATCH, OBLIGATION_MASKING, TEMP_TOKEN_EXPIRED)
- policy_evaluator_id: string (which policy engine evaluated)
- policy_version: string
- obligation_flags: list (comma-separated) e.g., "masking,watermark"
- requestor_claims: base64(jwt_claims) OR structured string (redact secrets)
- provenance_chain: semicolon-separated entries describing producers and transforms, e.g., "producer:svc-collector-1@2025-01-10T12:02Z|transform:redact-v1|store:artifact-bucket/a/2025-01-10"

Sample audit event (as string snippet for SIEM):
{
  "ts": "2025-01-20T18:12:01Z",
  "actor": "alice@example.com",
  "action": "evidence:download",
  "evidence_id": "ev-9f3b2c",
  "control_id": "CTL-4012",
  "resource_tenant": "tenant-83b2",
  "access_decision": "allow",
  "obligation_flags": "watermark,masking",
  "decision_reason": "RBAC_ALLOW_CONTROL_OWNER"
}

Collector behavior and obligations:
- On write: collector attachments must stamp artifact metadata with control_id, tenant_id, origin_producer and emit an audit event containing the new audit fields above.
- On read request proxied by collector: collector calls policy engine with (principal_claims, resource_attrs) and must act on obligations returned. Obligation examples:
  - must_mask: redact PII fields before returning artifact URL/content
  - must_watermark: insert watermark metadata into returned artifact or as an overlay link
  - log_full_context: include full requestor_claims in internal audit stream (not SIEM)
- On denied access: collector should emit a deny audit event with decision_reason and increment an internal metric collector.auth.deny and return standardized HTTP 403 with a small set of codes (see below).

Access decision HTTP mapping (collector API):
- 200: success (include signed, time-limited URL if download allowed)
- 403 + code "RBAC_DENY_SCOPE_MISMATCH"
- 403 + code "RBAC_DENY_ATTR_VIOLATION"
- 401 + code "TOKEN_EXPIRED"
- 429 for rate limit scenarios (still emit audit event)

SIEM export considerations:
- Exports must be tenant-aware. For hosted SIEM feeds, we should support per-tenant export configurations and a global redaction policy.
- Field-level redaction before pushing to customer SIEMs: PII should be removed unless customer explicit config allows it and RBAC allowed. Default: remove PII for evidence_tier != low.
- Export filters: only export events where (tenant_id in configured_tenants) AND (access_decision != deny OR include_denies_flag=true).
- For enterprise customers with on-prem SIEM: offer a signed envelope option that includes a short policy_summary to allow offline verification of scope.

Control evidence lifecycle and retention gating:
- Evidence states: created -> validated -> attested -> archived -> purged
- Retention gating rule: evidence cannot be purged until all active attestations are older than retention_cutoff OR have explicit revocation. Platform must surface attestations in the artifact metadata.
- RBAC integration: only principals with evidence:delete AND role:compliance-admin AND possession of a "delete_justification" claim may call purge. Purge should be logged with decision_reason=RBAC_ALLOW_PURGE_JUSTIFIED.

Operational workflows (short narratives):
1) Control owner requests a historical evidence download for audit:
   - Principal (alice) requests via Console -> console proxy includes JWT claims -> collector evaluates policy -> obligation: must_watermark -> collector returns signed URL and emits allow event with watermark obligation flag
   - Console displays a short attestation checkbox for download logging (ui side)
2) External auditor (tenant-authorized) requests scoped evidence snapshot for a quarter:
   - Auditor role = tenant-auditor + auditor:true attribute -> allowed view-only -> collector emits partial artifact (preview only) with redacted fields, SIEM records an export request (export_configured true)
3) Automated evidence attestation pipeline attempts to mark evidence as validated:
   - Pipeline service identity svc-attestor calls evidence:attest -> policy allows if svc-attestor in attestor_group AND control_id matches service's allowed_controls -> attestation entry appended to artifact provenance and audit event emitted

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Stale claims: tokens issued pre-RBAC-policy-change may incorrectly allow access. Mitigation: policy_version check in audit event and collector may require claims_issued_at > policy_effective_at; otherwise reject with decision_reason=STALE_CLAIMS
- Cross-tenant admin use: tool built for platform admins must use an explicit "breakglass" justification flow with extra MFA and audit hooks; these events must be labeled 'breakglass' and routed to a separate SIEM feed for SOC review
- Bulk export requests: collectors should rate-limit and convert to asynchronous job with signed artifact bundle and separate audit events for job start/finish to avoid streaming huge artifacts through the proxy

Implementation notes / API contract snippets (proto-like, described in plain text):
- Policy evaluation input: principal_claims (jwt), resource_attrs (evidence_id, control_id, tenant_id, evidence_tier), requested_action (evidence:download)
- Policy evaluation output: decision (allow|deny), obligation_flags (csv), policy_version, evaluator_id
- Collector must include policy_version and evaluator_id in emitted audit event for traceability

Standardized audit codes (short list):
- RBAC_ALLOW_CONTROL_OWNER
- RBAC_DENY_SCOPE_MISMATCH
- RBAC_DENY_ATTR_VIOLATION
- TOKEN_EXPIRED
- STALE_CLAIMS
- OBLIGATION_MASKING
- OBLIGATION_WATERMARK
- PURGE_JUSTIFIED

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should evidence_tier drive default masking policy or should masking policy be per-control? (Tradeoff: central policy easier, per-control gives control owners more granular protection)
- How do we represent transforms in provenance_chain for multi-step pipelines (suggestion: canonical transform ids + versions)?
- Do we allow requestor_claims to flow into tenant SIEM exports? (privacy risk)

Next steps / action items:
- (Priya) Draft minimal policy set for RBAC v2 that covers common roles (due 2025-02-10) - JIRA: SECD-4782
- (Ethan) Implement audit schema changes in platform middleware + unit tests (due 2025-02-28) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289
- (Maya) Update collector reference impl to call policy engine and enforce obligations (due 2025-03-12)
- (Security) Run tabletop for breakglass flow and SIEM export redaction rules (schedule in #security-ops)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive on obligations so collectors have deterministic behavior. If you want looser control, propose exact obligation shapes rather than free-form strings.
- Please cross-reference the RBAC v2 spec in Confluence (link above) when suggesting policy mapping changes.

Historical context / references:
- Previous evidence automation playbook (older): evidence-automation-playbook-and-siem-export-spec - this doc assumes some of those ideas but focuses on formalizing RBAC binding to evidence operations.
